title: The Tao (Yami) people of Lanyu and the flying fish calendar

sources.publisher: Marine National Park Headquarters, Ministry of the Interior (Taiwan)

facts.text: The Tao (Yami) people live on Lanyu (Orchid Island), in Taitung County off the southeast coast of Taiwan.
The Tao divide the year into three seasons according to flying fish harvesting.
When the coral trees bloom, the flying fish season begins, roughly from February to June; the fish arrive with the Kuroshio Current.
Each village holds a ceremony on the shore to call the fish and announce the start of the season.
During the season men catch flying fish and other migratory fish but do not catch coral reef or bottom-dwelling fish; women clean and dry the catch.
From about July to September, after the flying fish season, reef fish may be caught.
November to January is the season of waiting for the flying fish.
According to the Marine National Park Headquarters, these seasonal limits have helped many species on Lanyu keep reproducing.
Traditional Tao boats are painted with red, black and white patterns.
During the flying fish season visitors should not climb onto traditional boats casually for photos.
Visitors are asked not to bring oranges to the seaside, especially during the flying fish season.
Flying fish are dried on racks and later stored in pottery jars for the months after the season.

notes: 選文沒有阿拉伯數字；月份與季節對照 f3、f6、f7。文本 B 是虛構的遊記體裁，所寫的規矩與景象都對得到 f9–f12。
